edits.find: The infection history only establishes that this is a primary immunodeficiency rather than ordinary toddler illness — ICU-level pneumococcal pneumonia, tympanic perforation with otorrhea, and weight below the 3rd percentile clear that bar. The actual fork is decided by one line of the panel: IgM 450 against IgG 250 and IgA 24. Every other option on the list requires IgM to be low (XLA), low or normal (CVID), normal (selective IgA deficiency, Job), or accompanied by a non-immunologic finding this child does not have (Wiskott-Aldrich's microthrombocytopenia, HIV's inverted CD4/CD8). An isolated elevation of IgM with everything downstream absent is class-switch failure — CD40 ligand on the T cell cannot engage CD40 on the B cell, so the B cell stays locked on its native isotype. The neutropenia (15% of 9,000) is the free confirmatory detail: it accompanies CD40L deficiency and does not belong to XLA or CVID.

edits.find: Two features settle this and both are anatomical. First, the lesions are vesicles and ulcers, not exudate, which removes every bacterial and mononucleosis-type pharyngitis at a stroke, since adenovirus, EBV and S. pyogenes all produce tonsillar exudate and none produces oral vesicles. Second, and this is the whole question, the lesions are posterior — soft palate, uvula, anterior palatine pillars — with the tongue, lips and buccal mucosa explicitly spared. Herpangina, from coxsackievirus A, lives in the back of the mouth; herpetic gingivostomatitis lives in the front, with red swollen gums. The stem spares exactly the structures HSV would involve.

edits.find: Two findings name the defect and neither is the pneumonia. Granulomas on biopsy and a Burkholderia cepacia culture together point at one disease: chronic granulomatous disease, a disorder of NADPH oxidase, commonly X-linked with autosomal recessive forms. The enzyme drives the neutrophil respiratory burst, so its loss means decreased superoxide production — phagocytes migrate normally and ingest normally, but have impaired intracellular killing. The organism list follows directly: neutrophils can borrow hydrogen peroxide made by the pathogen itself, so susceptibility particularly involves characteristic catalase-positive organisms that destroy their own peroxide; this is not an exclusive organism list. The granulomas are the same defect seen histologically: phagocytes arrive but clear pathogens poorly, contributing to granuloma formation.
